# `Receive`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Updater: result of a binary upload received on the updater's binary socket.

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | event (device sends) |
| Grade | PURE GETTER (observation only) |
| Side-effect tier | B |
| Confidence | READ |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.31, updater socket_json_server::NotifyRecv @0x12c20 and socket_json_server_binary::NotifyRecv @0x28240 (64-bit build); 32-bit counterparts present; per-IP send adds route; state strings in networkThread @0xf150 |

Sent by the updater's binary receiver when a firmware upload on the binary transfer socket (TCP 4361) ends; the notification travels on TCP 4350, not on 4361. Sent by the updater process (zwoair_updater) on its TCP 4350 JSON server, not by the imager. Delivered with an IP-matched send: every 4350 connection whose IP string equals the target's receives it, so several sockets from one host can all match, and other clients get nothing. State: complete on success, otherwise one of recv interrupted, timeout, recv timeout, md5 verify_fail, verify_fail or verify_fail: sign (READ). A 4361 receive idle for about 10 s is ended. On the successful path a complete Receive precedes the installation progress Update events; that is not a guarantee a disconnected client receives it. Updater custom producer: no code or error member. Android app consumer (READ, consumer expectation): the legacy firmware-upload screen treats any Receive whose state is not complete as a failure. The newer app OTA workflow listens for a different name (OtaUpdate); no emitter for it was found in either packaged updater build.

Side effects: Observation only for the receiver.

## Request params

None. Events are sent by the device without a request; the payload is below.

## Payload

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Event` | string | yes | - | Discriminator. Fixed value `"Receive"`. [READ] |
| `Timestamp` | string | yes | - | Decimal string <seconds>.<nine digits> from clock id 1 (monotonic, INFERRED); not a calendar time. [READ] |
| `state` | string | yes | - | complete on success; any other value is a failure (MD5 mismatch, signature failure, interruption or timeout). One of: `complete`, `recv interrupted`, `timeout`, `recv timeout`, `md5 verify_fail`, `verify_fail`, `verify_fail: sign`. [READ] |
| `route` | array<string> | yes | - | Always an empty array, inserted by the IP-matched sender. It is not function ancestry and does not carry the recipient IP. [READ] |

## Errors

None. Failures appear in the payload (`code`, `error`) when `state` is `fail`.

## Example

Event, complete - Static example of the success path (READ shape, not captured):

```json
{"Event":"Receive","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","state":"complete","route":[]}
```
